newsitem.title: ITALY: Van Miert says Italy will implement Omnitel accord. [CORRECTED 01:13 GMT 13/9]
newsitem.headline: Van Miert says Italy will implement Omnitel accord. [CORRECTED 01:13 GMT 13/9]

text.p: The Italian government has promised to implement a 1995 accord which offered compensation to Italy's second mobile phone operator Omnitel, European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Tuesday.

Omnitel, controlled by troubled information technology group Olivetti, complained to the European Commission that it was charged a fee of 750 billion lire by the Italian government in 1994 to enter the cellular phone market.
State operator Telecom Italia Mobile was not charged a similar fee.
The government late last year reached a deal with the European Commission to allow Omnitel to compete on equal terms with TIM, but this accord has not yet been fully honoured.
Van Miert met Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico on Tuesday to discuss the accord, and told reporters afterwards he was satisified by the meeting.
"The minister will be able to implement the agreement," Van Miert said.
As part of the deal the government said Omnitel would receive a 25 percent reduction in connection fees to state-controlled telephone lines in 1996 and another 25 percent reduction in 1997.
This should save Omnitel some 60 billion lire over this period.

In addition Omnitel will be given a concession to set up a DCS 1800 standard Personal Communications Network (PCN) mobile phone network. However it will not be able to start operating the new system until a third mobile phone licence is awarded and in any case not before December 31, 1998.

Olivetti has a 41.3 percent stake in the Omnitel consortium, which also includes the U.S. operators Bell Atlantic Corp and Airtouch Communications and Germany's Mannesmann. (Corrects to make clear that Airtouch Communications has replaced Pacific Telesis as a partner) -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
